synopsis: ISO 21815-1:2022, dated January 2022, covers detection, operator warning, automatic intervention and testing for earth-moving, mobile underground mining and road-construction machinery; the booklet identifies it as the clearest scope match for an OEM-fitted warning-plus-automatic-braking system, but excludes systems installed before publication [f6741, f381, f2154, f2153]. Its permitted interventions are speed reduction, stopping and motion inhibition—not automatic steering—and responsibility remains with the operator because the technology cannot cover every situation [f11701, f11702, f3647]. Clause 6 specifies physical performance tests with pass/fail criteria and false-positive tests, which the project is advised to retain for each scenario class [f7726, f7884]. The review found neither provisions accepting simulation evidence nor statistical acceptance targets, sample sizes or simulation-credibility rules; however, the full paid texts could not be checked, so failure to find simulation substitution does not establish that it is prohibited [f9780, f11237, f324, f6749, f7544]. Functional standardization does not establish quantified field effectiveness or second-order hazards, and the research evidence is concentrated in surface mining and construction despite the standard's underground-machinery coverage [f3443, f1164].
